title: Redemption
definition: Redemption is God's rescue of sinners from bondage and guilt through the price paid by Jesus Christ.
summary: Redemption is Christ's purchase of sinners out of bondage by the price of His blood.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Redeemer who gives Himself as the ransom for sinners and liberates them for God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Redemption uses the language of ransom, liberation, and ownership. Sinners are not merely mistaken; they are enslaved to sin and unable to free themselves. Christ redeems by paying the price and claiming His people as His own.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because salvation is freedom with a new Master, not independence from God. Redemption shows both the cost of grace and the believer's new belonging. It confronts every false freedom that leaves people enslaved to sin.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live as one bought by Christ rather than owned by old chains. Bring areas of bondage under His lordship and ask for grace to walk free. Let gratitude for the price paid shape worship, purity, and service.
